lastText: File ClosedA Record Argued For, Not AssumedMinor DefeatItalian High Command, 1940 — 1945End of hostilities: MAY 2, 1945 — filed late, out of sequenceImmediate AftermathArmy Group C surrenders in Italy on May 2, 1945, five days before the wider European war ends — the close of nineteen months fighting as a junior Allied partner on Italian soil. The human cost of this path runs higher than the historical one at nearly every hinge point — Italy's own wartime dead, roughly 300,000 military and civilian combined split across two governments and a country fought over twice, were already among the higher tolls of any Axis power relative to population. The delay meant to buy Rome a coordinated defense instead bought German intelligence two additional days to reinforce the garrison — Operation Achse executed even more completely than its historical version. Rome pressed Berlin and Madrid for a seat in the Gibraltar question rather than settling for Malta or Egypt alone — a diplomatic wager the documented record never records Italy attempting, win or lose at Hendaye's actual table. A deliberate early withdrawal from the Alamein line concedes the same ground the historical twelve-day battle eventually lost anyway, without first spending the attritional casualties a fuel-starved defense was never favored to hold.
